brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut — they keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms, and their cash is stuck for 104 days vs 79 days, so they'll value faster payment.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price cut on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Benchmark to the market-fair band of ₹0.65–0.80/pc for 28 mm caps at higher volume
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms — that extra margin gives room to cut price. Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (15 days after receipt instead of 30) in exchange for part of the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹22.57 L of our cash, but it's worth about 12.19% per year to them (what they pay to borrow money) — so trade some of that saving for a deeper price cut

brief.financialLeverage: They're healthy — CRISIL A+ / Stable rating, making ₹937.60 Cr revenue and keeping 5.9% profit (vs 3.8% for peers). But their cash is stuck for 104 days vs 79 days for similar firms, meaning cash is tighter for them than it looks. We're only 0.59% of their revenue, so we're a small customer — but their fast growth (22.1%/yr from the levers) means they want new business. Push hard on price using the profit gap; offer faster payment to sweeten the deal and unlock their cash crunch.

evidence.point: They keep more profit than similar firms
Their cash is stuck longer than similar firms
They already take longer to pay their own suppliers than most
We are a small customer to them
They borrow money at about 12.19% per year
Paying 15 days faster frees up cash for us

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health B (65/100) — a strong second source

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma) — strong, profitable, robust alternate for bottles/closures

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle/jar specialist (Pearlpet) — direct fit for PET bottles

risks: We're only 0.59% of their revenue — a small customer — so we have limited clout; lead with the profit-gap data and the faster-payment offer to make the ask compelling.

Their Altman Z-score is 2.17 (grey zone) — not distress, but not rock-solid either. Don't squeeze so hard that you destabilize a supplier; keep the tone collaborative and frame faster payment as a win for them.
They have a strong credit rating (CRISIL A+ / Stable), so they won't feel desperate — build the case on the profit gap and market benchmarks, not on financial pressure.
Market asking price shows modest headroom (₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume) — the 10–15% cut is at the edge of that band, so be ready to show volume commitment or spec flexibility to justify it.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about aligning your pricing with the market and with what similar firms are keeping as profit — we see room for a better deal, and we're ready to help your cash flow by paying faster.
